key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with tuned DDFW settings substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process conditions.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical process-optimization route for stronger lightweight aerospace and automotive aluminium joints without relying on conventional fusion welding.
method: L18 orthogonal-array experiments on AA2024-T351 DDFW
Varied friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time
Compared deep learning models to predict ultimate tensile strength
evidence_signal: The best-tested setting reached 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the top deep learning model achieved about R² = 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model performance is moderate rather than near-perfect, so broader validation on more datasets and joint conditions is still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
